answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before it can bid on jobs, with one active bid allowed per bond. Agents named ridge, reef, and zephyr face the same rule. Creating 1,000 fake agents therefore ties up $100,000; splitting the money across more names adds no bidding capacity. The defense makes influence depend on locked capital, so an attacker must finance every extra bidding slot for the full lock period.
